title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District
area: South-central Pennsylvania, including Cumberland and Dauphin (Harrisburg) counties and part of York County.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground, and as of July 2026 major election forecasters rated it a Toss-up. Scott Perry won re-election 53.8%-46.2% in 2022 and defeated Janelle Stelson 50.5%-49.3% in 2024, when Donald Trump (R) carried the district 52.0%-46.8% over Kamala Harris. As of June 30, 2026, Perry had raised $5.19 million and Stelson had raised $6.36 million.

PoliticsPA's Louis Jacobson wrote that Perry was the most vulnerable House Republican incumbent on the 2026 ballot: "he has articulated the most conservative views of the four vulnerable Republicans on our list despite representing a district that went to Donald Trump in 2024 by a modest five points ... Republicans paint Perry as a survivor."

Janelle Stelson defeated Justin Douglas in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary; Scott Perry was unopposed in the Republican primary. Isabelle Harman (Independent) did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

summary.text: Scott Perry is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 10th District, first elected in 2012. He is a retired Pennsylvania Army National Guard brigadier general, co-founded a mechanical contracting firm, and served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives before Congress. He serves on the House Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure, Foreign Affairs, Oversight and Government Reform, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and is a former chairman of the House Freedom Caucus.

background.text: Born in San Diego, California, in 1962. According to his official biography, he is the grandson of Colombian immigrants and the son of a single mother who settled the family in the Harrisburg area and then Dillsburg; he began working at age 13 as a fruit picker.

Graduated from Northern High School and the Cumberland-Perry Vo-Tech School in 1980, then earned a B.S. in business administration management from Pennsylvania State University in 1991 while working full-time. He later earned a master's degree in strategic studies from the U.S. Army War College.

Enlisted in the Army in 1980 and was commissioned a second lieutenant through Officer Candidate School. A helicopter pilot, he commanded a National Guard aviation battalion that deployed to Iraq in 2009-2010, became a colonel in 2011, was promoted to brigadier general in 2014, and retired on March 1, 2019, after serving as Assistant Adjutant General.

Before politics, worked as a mechanic, dock worker, draftsman and licensed insurance agent. In 1993 he and his mother started a mechanical contracting firm in Dillsburg that served utilities in several states.
Chaired the Carroll Township Planning Commission, then served three terms in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, leaving in 2012.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2012. He won re-election in 2022 with 53.8% of the vote and defeated Janelle Stelson 50.5%-49.3% in 2024.

Serves on the House Committees on Transportation and Infrastructure (where he chairs the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management), Foreign Affairs, Oversight and Government Reform, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. His official biography describes him as an early member and former chairman of the House Freedom Caucus.

priorities.text: Campaign describes him as bringing "a diverse background in business, military, and community service" to Congress, citing nearly 40 years in the military and his work commanding units in Iraq.
priorities.quote: He started working at 13 and co-founded a mechanical contracting firm. With nearly 40 years in the military, he achieved the rank of Brigadier General, commanding units in Iraq and earning a Master's in Strategic Studies from the U.S. Army War College.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign issues page says he opposes "Medicare for All" and single-payer health care and extending Social Security or Medicare benefits to non-U.S. citizens.
positions.quote: He is opposed to the socialist "Medicare for All" and single-payer healthcare, and any attempt to provide illegals and non-U.S. citizens with Social Security and/or Medicare benefits.

positions.summary: His official site says banning firearms does not address the root cause of violence and that the federal government has limited authority to regulate gun rights.
positions.quote: Attempting to stop acts of violence by banning firearms doesn’t address the root cause of the violence.

positions.summary: His official site says he supports the Supreme Court decision returning abortion decisions to the states and that any law should include exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother.
positions.quote: The U.S. Supreme Court ensured that states can now make decisions regarding abortion - the termination of innocent lives - and I support the court’s decision.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign issues page says he opposes requiring schools to allow athletes who identify as female to compete in women’s sports.
positions.quote: As the father of two daughters, Scott opposes any attempt to allow males to compete against females in women’s sports.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (chairing the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee), and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Janelle Stelson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Justin Douglas

summary.text: Janelle Stelson is a former television journalist who spent 26 years at WGAL-TV in central Pennsylvania, including as a news anchor. She was the Democratic nominee in 2024, when she lost to Scott Perry by about one percentage point, and is running again in 2026. She has focused her campaign on affordability, health care, and measures to address government corruption such as term limits and a congressional stock-trading ban.

background.text: Born in Fairbanks, Alaska, and grew up in the Seattle area of Washington.
Earned a B.A. in politics and government from the University of Puget Sound.
Her first job was writing speeches for the Egyptian embassy in Washington, D.C., before her broadcast career.
Worked in television news in central Pennsylvania for more than 30 years, according to her campaign website, including 26 years as a news anchor, reporter and weather anchor at WGAL-TV.

Ran for Congress in 2024 as the Democratic nominee in the 10th District and lost to Perry by 5,133 votes (Perry received 50.6%), the narrowest margin Perry had faced since his first election in 2012. She was living just outside the district at the time.

Announced on July 14, 2025, that she would run again, and said she then lived in Cumberland County, within the district. She won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 67.4% of the vote over Justin Douglas.
Her campaign website says she supports term limits, including for herself, and a ban on members of Congress trading stocks.

priorities.text: Says Central Pennsylvanians are being squeezed by rising costs while Perry "supports the chaotic policy of ever-changing tariff-taxes that raise prices and kill jobs" and was "the deciding vote on a budget that slashes food assistance, raises utility bills and adds $3.4 trillion dollars in new debt."
priorities.quote: Central Pennsylvanians are working harder than ever and falling further behind. We are being squeezed by the rising cost of everything from groceries to health care.

priorities.text: Proposes a congressional ethics plan including 12-year term limits for herself, a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks, a lifetime lobbying ban for former members, and a stronger, independent Congressional Ethics Agency.
priorities.quote: Limit terms to 12 years. Even if Congress does not act to require term limits, I will limit my own terms and will not serve more than 12 years.

priorities.text: Says she supports high-quality, affordable health care with better access to urgent and primary care, and opposes surprise medical billing.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, saying she would repeal what she calls Perry's "tariff taxes" that are increasing costs.
positions.quote: I will repeal these tariff taxes that are increasing costs and vote to end the war in Iran.

positions.summary: Supports tax breaks for the "hard-working middle class, not billionaires," and opposes continuing tax breaks for the wealthy and a proposed new national sales tax.
positions.quote: I support tax breaks for the hard-working middle class, not billionaires.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page says she will fight to restore the protections of Roe v. Wade as federal law.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will fight to ensure the protections guaranteed under Roe are once again the law of the land.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; ran unsuccessfully for this seat in 2024.

sources.title: Janelle Stelson renews campaign to oust Scott Perry from Congress
